judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Adequate insurance coverage' is undefined but the paragraph is descriptive risk disclosure rather than covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c069 imposes the actual insurance condition; this risk factor cross-refers to nothing that fails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long conditional description ('should such an inter-creditor agreement be in place ... the Company would expect') with no operative commitment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c079's reference to inter-creditor agreements and c062's junior-lien limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes equity-pledge collateral risk in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c060 permits indirect loan investment through an entity interest, which this describes rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable efforts in reliance on qualified advisors' is a soft standard, but the clause imposes no enforceable duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeats c133 nearly verbatim; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Usury risk stated as an expectation ('is expected to comply'); nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c132 covers the same ground for the Notes themselves and reaches the same conclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence to a conflicts list, expressly non-exhaustive ('include, but are not limited to').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Frames c157-c159 and echoes c049 without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive of competing time demands; 'sufficient resources and time' is soft but not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c056 and c110 state the actual time commitment in two different formulations, which this risk factor reflects.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proportionally greater than the Interest payable to Noteholders' is an unquantified comparison, and the heading 'Proportionally Disproportionate' is itself confused.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Manager and members 'will receive Company gains', which is consistent with c112's allocation of all tax items to Members but sits against c098's minimal $25,000 contribution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general conflicts description closing with an exhortation; no operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers correctly to Section III Conflicts of Interest (c049 et seq.).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introduces 'risks that are typical of investments in private equity funds' although the Notes are debt, which is a loose characterisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c018, c112 and c123 insist the Noteholders hold debt and no equity interest, so the private-equity framing sits oddly with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'It has no operating history and has not identified all of its portfolio loans' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the promotional track-record recitals at c022, c023 and c025 — the recital-versus-disclosure tension the Memorandum carries throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May become concentrated in a limited number of portfolio loans' is descriptive, with no threshold stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c077 caps single-loan commitments at 20% of capital only 'after the second year of the Company's term', so this risk factor discloses the gap that provision leaves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blind-pool risk stated plainly; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c060's guidelines and c161.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'There is no assurance that the Noteholders' security interest will be perfected in seniority' is candid but internally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly undercuts c012 and c018's unqualified statements that the Notes are secured by the Company's assets and that Noteholders 'will be secured creditors', and works with c108's senior borrowing consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Severely restricted' is a characterisation rather than a rule, with the actual restriction located elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c107 states the operative restriction with exceptions for family trusts and affiliates, which this absolute-sounding sentence does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Illiquidity described definitely; the representation requirement is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c017, c181 and c004's legend.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Precludes the Noteholders from active participation ... or from voting on Company operating matters' is stated absolutely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c109 in fact gives a Majority in Interest of Noteholders veto rights over mergers, liens, salaries and the Manager's withdrawal, and c114 requires their approval for amendments — so the flat 'no voting' statement is hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Key-man risk described in ordinary terms; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c084 (additional or substitute managers) and c027.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A summary risk paragraph directing investors to their own advisors; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers accurately to Section VI (c119-c134).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Manager believes' is a belief, not a covenant; the text is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the Investment Company Act of 1940 as the 'Company Act', a third label for a statute already defined as the 'Investment Company Act' at c003 and c130, and 'Company Act' risks confusion with the 'Company Agreement' at c081.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closing exhortation and disclaimer; no operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces c026 against the promotional recitals at c012 and c022.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Certain eligibility and suitability standards' is unspecific in the stem, though the following paragraphs supply the content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires suitability to be met again at the time of an 'Interest Roll-over Request', which c089 conditions only on being 'a qualified investor' — a term not used in Section VIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stem sentence tying the representations to Rule 501; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces c174-c179 coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reasonable-expectation clause at the end could attach to either the joint income or both income tests, and 'net worth ... within the meaning of such terms as used in' Rule 501 imports an external and changing standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c088's accredited-investor gate; no other provision restates the individual test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limiting the trust category to an 'IRREVOCABLE TRUST' with $5,000,000 in assets is narrower than Rule 501 and, read with the other enumerated categories, invites an expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c179 separately admits 'a living trust or other revocable trust' whose grantors and trustees qualify, and c088 refers to individuals' 'estate planning vehicles' — three different treatments of trusts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'INVESTMENT COMPANY registered under the United States Companies Act of 1940' misnames the Investment Company Act and then defines that misnomer as 'the Companies Act'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same statute is called the 'Investment Company Act' at c003 and c130 and the 'Company Act' at c170, so the instrument uses three different names for it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'gither' is a typographical error for 'either', and the (B) limb runs two alternatives together so it is unclear whether the self-directed proviso qualifies the asset test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c128-c129 address plan investors substantively without contradicting these thresholds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not formed for the purpose of acquiring the Note' is a qualifier that may or may not extend to the 501(c)(3) limb that follows it in the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c180 then provides for entities that were formed to purchase a Note, which cannot satisfy this clause — the two paragraphs describe overlapping but inconsistent gates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause qualifies by reference to 'clause (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) or (v) above or this clause (vi)', a self-referential definition that can recurse without limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c175 it admits revocable trusts that c175 excludes, so the two eligibility limbs are in tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short look-through requirement for entities formed to purchase a Note; the mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c178 requires the entity 'not formed for the purpose of acquiring the Note', so the two paragraphs set up an unexplained overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Solely for the investor's own account and not directly or indirectly for the account of any other person whatsoever' is absolute, softened only by the trustee parenthesis.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c088 contemplates purchases through 'estate planning vehicles' and c179 through entities owned by accredited investors, which strain 'own account'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional sophistication and risk-bearing representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c166 and c172.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sole and absolute discretion' to accept or reject is deliberately unbounded but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c005 and c088; the actor is the Manager here whereas c081 says the 'Managing Member'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without unreasonable effort or expense' is a familiar and workable qualifier on the information right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Substantially repeats c007's promise of access to management; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes the Memorandum as 'a general outline' 'necessarily incomplete', and refers to 'its Managing Member' although the Company has a Manager and Members.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Memorandum is qualified in its entirety by the Note Purchase Agreement, while c009 says it is qualified by the whole set of Offering Documents including the Operating Agreement; and 'Managing Member' recurs only at c081.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contact details only; nothing capable of construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c184's direction to address questions to the Principals.
